sql:
SELECT COUNT(1) AS n
FROM   TPCDS_DB.store_sales ss
LEFT JOIN TPCDS_DB.promotion p ON ss.ss_promo_sk = p.p_promo_sk
WHERE  ss.ss_customer_sk IS NULL

attempts.sql: SELECT COUNT(1) AS n FROM TPCDS_DB.store_sales ss WHERE ss.ss_customer_sk IS NULL
attempts.change_summary: Removed unnecessary LEFT JOIN to promotion since no promotion columns are referenced and p_promo_sk is unique, so the join cannot change the row count.

diagnosis.bottleneck: The query scans store_sales for rows where ss_customer_sk IS NULL and then performs a left outer join to promotion, but the join is unnecessary because promotion.p_promo_sk is unique and no columns from promotion are used in the output; the join adds broadcast, hash build, and probe overhead on top of the scan.

plan_nodes.note: LeftOuter BuildRight; Left keys [1]: [ss_promo_sk#48427]; Right keys [1]: [p_promo_sk#48442]; Join type: LeftOuter; Join

hypotheses.claim: A LEFT JOIN whose columns are never read still costs a join; if the joined key is unique it cannot change the rows and can be removed. (matched: left join tpcds_db.promotion p on ss.ss_promo_sk = p.p_promo_sk)

The BroadcastHashJoin (left outer) is redundant: the right side (promotion) has a unique key (p_promo_sk) and no promotion columns are referenced, so removing the join would eliminate the broadcast exchange, hash table build, and probe without changing the result.

The Parquet scan of store_sales with pushed IsNull predicate still reads all row groups containing null ss_customer_sk; if the fraction of nulls is high, this scan dominates runtime, but the join adds additional per-row processing cost.
The Filter node simply passes through rows after the scan's predicate pushdown; its cost is negligible compared to the scan and join.
